topic: placing fractions with denominators 2, 3, 4, 6 and 8 on number lines
subtitle: Naming the fraction at a marked point, placing a fraction on a partitioned line, and comparing two fractions on the line

problems.note: 0 to 1 cut into 2 equal parts; point A sits on the first tick after 0.
0 to 1 cut into 4 equal parts; point B is 3 parts from 0.

traps.desc: counted the tick marks instead of the equal parts, so the point was read as 3 out of 5

problems.note: 0 to 1 cut into 3 equal parts; point C is 2 parts from 0.

traps.desc: counted the parts to the right of the point instead of counting from 0

problems.note: Student marks 4/6 on a sixths line, then names the same point with a simpler fraction.
Marking 8/8 lands on the whole number 1.

traps.desc: thought a fraction can never reach a whole number and stopped one eighth short

problems.note: Same numerator, different denominators: thirds are longer parts than fourths.
Both marked on one eighths line; 3/4 lands on the sixth tick.
Line runs 0 to 2 in halves; point D is 3 halves from 0.

traps.desc: read the line as if it ended at 1, so the point was called 3 out of 4 ticks

problems.note: Marks 5/3 on a 0-to-2 thirds line, then reports how far past 1 it sits.

traps.desc: gave the whole distance from 0 instead of the distance past 1

problems.desc: Error analysis: mark 1/3 and 1/2 on two matched number lines and explain in a sentence why a larger denominator makes a smaller unit fraction. Open written explanation - manual review.
